utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Good morning to you all. Judge Parker is unable to sit today, so again Judge Thelin and myself will sit alone. Before we start with the witness I understand that Mr. Tarculovski has to make a submission through Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if we could go to a private session for a brief period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Yes, private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. May I ask you to read the affirmation is on the card before you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the record, the Prosecution is calling the witness Dr. Klaus Stein, witness number M 166.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Stein. Just for the record is your name Dr. Klaus Stein?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Could you please briefly describe your educational and professional background.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: I finished my school studies in 1981 and then I served in the army for 15 months and then studied chemistry, and in -- five years later I graduated and then I finished my doctorate in this subject, and two months after finishing my doctorate, I began working as an expert for chemistry at the Bavarian police. My speciality are explosives and drugs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you're currently employed with the Bavarian place at this time?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, that was my first job and I'm still there as civilian servant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And on 24 February 2006, did you prepare a report which contained your expert opinion on two particular questions, the first being: What origins may be causal for nitrate or nitrite deposits on the hands of persons? And the second question being: Is it possible that persons have nitrate or nitrite deposits on their hands if they have previously been exposed to the reaction clouds of military explosives or if they have manual contact with objects being exposed to the reaction clouds. Did you prepare a report regarding these issues?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, we have prepared binders for Dr. Stein's testimony and with the usher's assistance, we'd like to distribute those now. Now, can we please show the witness 65 ter 361, which is also at tab 2 of today's binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Dr. Stein, on the screen in front of you you will see the first page of a document and you have the entire document in front of you at tab 2. The document that is in front of you, is this the report that you prepared on 24 February 2006?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, that is my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And does this report also have attached to it a series of photographs?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Can we please show 65 ter 362 which is at tab 3 of the witness binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Dr. Stein, the photographs that you have in front of you, do you recognise these as being the attachment to your report of 24 February 2006?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And were these photographs referenced and relied upon in your report?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This is the diphenylamine test.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honours, I would seek to tender the report which is 65 ter 361 as well as the attachment which is 65 ter 362.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Dr. Stein, with regards to the first question --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 361 will become Exhibit P430 and 65 ter 362 will become Exhibit P431, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I apologise for jumping the gun there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Dr. Stein, with regards to the first question in your report, that is, the possible origins of nitrite/nitrate on the hands of persons you described using a diphenylamine test. Can you please explain, just in general terms, what that test involves and how it works?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: The diphenylamine test reacts to nitrate or nitrite with a colour reaction. The oxidization qualities of nitrates and nitrites are turned blue. The test is quite sensitive but not specific. Other substances cause the same reaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So to pick up on that point, Dr. Stein, you say that the diphenylamine test is not specific for nitrates and nitrites. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: What other substances would return a positive result from such a test?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: There are, for instance cleansing agents, with hypochlorites which is an oxidizer, this test would give a positive result because I've carried out such tests. Also, iron(III), a part of rust, component of rust, would have a positive result. Herbicides, for instance, with chlorates, which are still allowed in some countries but not in my country.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Stein. Now, with regards to your report, you referred to nitrates and nitrites. Can you explain whether there are any significant difference between nitrates and nitrites for purposes of the diphenylamine test?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: No, there's no difference for this test. The only difference would be in that there is one more part of the molecule added in the one, but the test has the same result.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So for the purposes of today's testimony if I refer only to one, for example, nitrates, your answer would be the name for nitrites?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And using only the diphenylamine test, can one establish with any degree of certainty whether a positive result is caused by the presence of nitrate particles?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: As I said, there are also other substances which would cause a positive reaction, so you couldn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And to take that one step further, again, using only the diphenylamine test can one establish with any degree of certainty whether a positive result was caused by gunpowder residue?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: One could say that it is possible with gunpowder residue but with other substances too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So to summarize what you have told us so far would it be correct to say that the diphenylamine test would more accurately be termed a pre-test for nitrites and nitrates?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: In Germany, is the diphenylamine test used to detect the presence of nitrites and nitrates?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: No. We have a more specific test, which is called Lang [phoen] reagent, in which substances are put into an ammonium salts substance. It's only for nitrite, where nitrate has to be altered before it could be used. But this test is much more sensitive.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: From the knowledge that you have at this time, are you aware of a procedure known as the paraffin glove test?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you know how the paraffin glove test is performed?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And does the paraffin glove test also use diphenylamine to detect the presence of nitrate particles?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, the paraffin test removes the particles and then the diphenylamine test is used for the reaction itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So the paraffin glove test also uses diphenylamine; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And would the paraffin glove test be subject to the same limitations have you described already for the diphenylamine test?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And are you aware that in 2001 the paraffin glove test was the method used by the Macedonian police to test for the presence of nitrates on the hands of persons?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, I read about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, could we please display for the doctor Exhibit P0050 which is also 65 ter number 15.7. It is located in tab 6 of today's binder, and in e-court it's at page 25 in English, and page 101 in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And just before we go on that document I would like to turn back to something you said earlier. Page 6, I asked you about whether it could be established with any degree the certainty that gunshot residue is present from the diphenylamine test. If a test returned a positive result, could you say with certainty that this was caused by gunshot residue.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: No, you can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So that would just be one of a number of possibilities?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now turning to the document that's on the screen in front of you and that is also at tab 6 of the binder, I'll just run through it quickly with you. You'll see that at the top left it says, "Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Interior, criminological police, criminal techniques department." It's dated 27 August, 2001. It goes on to mention the names of particular individuals. Then in the third paragraph it states: "The detection of traces of gunpowder particles is done through identifying the nitrate particles they contain, a component of gunpowder, with the use of the identification reagent for nitrate, diphenylamine." Do you see that, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And then in the next paragraph it continues: "Regarding the number of sources in everyday life of a person where contamination with nitrate particles can occur, their presence on the hands of a person is an indication that that person has fired a fire-arm." Do you see that, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And the last paragraph reads: "Based on their form, location and position, it can be determined with a great probability that these nitrate particles originate from gunpowder." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Can we please look at another document now. This is Exhibit P0050 also. It is 65 ter number 15.8. It's in tab 7 of today's binder, and it's at e-court page 26 in English and page 102 in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Perhaps at this time I will continue with the -- just using the document that in the folder in front of you. Doctor, you'll see that this letter is almost identical to the previous document. Again it says Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Interior, it's dated 27 August 2001, and it's addressed to Basic Court Skopje II. And, Doctor, can you see from looking at it that the last three paragraphs are identical to the last three paragraphs of the previous document you saw?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if can we can leave this document up for the doctor to refer to. Can we go back to paragraph 3 of this document. There is the paragraph starting: "The detection of traces of gunpowder particles, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: To put this paragraph in the context of what you have already stated, using the diphenylamine test alone, can one determine whether a substance is a nitrate particle?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Well, one can't, of course. It could be nitrate, but it could be a couple of other things as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if we move on now to the fourth paragraph I would ask you to focus on that, and there it states: "Regarding the limited number of sources in everyday life of a person where contamination with nitrate particles can occur ... " and so on, Doctor, based on your training and experience would you agree with this statement that in the course of one's everyday life there's little likelihood that a person would come into contact with substances containing nitrates?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: No, quite the opposite, that does not reflect what we have learned in our forensic training that when there is a positive colour result you can immediately draw conclusions about this possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And in the course of preparing your expert report, did you perform any experiments to test this out?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes. I used some chemicals from daily life, and a test with sterols also shows a positive result.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you recall what other substances, if any, returned positive results?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes. Well, cleaning agents, as I mentioned before, which contain hypochlorite; rust, which is a component that one can always be in contact with; weed killers; herbicides, they contain chlorates; fertiliser, especially -- several fertilisers, they're organic as well and are based on nitrates, and if one is in contact with fertiliser, then the positive will -- the test will always be positive; pottery with glazing, that has brown stone which a mild oxidant; manganese dioxide and there again the test would be positive; curing salts, that's based on nitrite, in small concentration so one wouldn't expect the test to be strongly positive, but there's sufficient of the substance there for there to be a clear-colour reaction. And then for the rest, they're only explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And is this an exhaustive list of all the possible substances that could produce a positive result?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: No. There are others. For example, I'm just thinking, because often we have false alarms at airports. There are a few types of perfume based on nitro-aromates, TNT is a nitro-aromate, and there the possibility of distinction, well, in airports you have to be really fast and it's difficult to make a distinction and if you use this -- if that substance goes through the detectors there is an immediate TNT alarm that goes off. I haven't been able to prove this, but based on the chemical composition and the basis is the same and therefore one would expect this test to be positive as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If I could just have one second. If we could show the recently admitted exhibit, 431. And this is in tab 3 of today's binder, and I'd ask that we go to page 20, which has ERN N002-5818. Sorry, it would be the page before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Doctor, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And what does this photograph show?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: That's the diphenylamine test with gunpowder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And the blue colour indicates a positive result?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, it does. In this case, strong positive reaction. At the bottom, you just see a light blue colouring, so the bottom part shows less of the substance present.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could we now go to page four of the same exhibit which is ERN N002-5803?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Doctor, what does this photograph show?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: That's the diphenylamine test with potassium chlorate which is a component of weed killer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this test also indicates a positive result; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And now could we go to page 1 of the same exhibit with ERN N002-5801.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Doctor, what substance is shown here in this test?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: That's a hypochlorite, a component of cleaning agents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, again, does the light blue colour here indicate a positive result?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And we could leave this exhibit up, I will be referring to other pages in it shortly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Doctor, as part of your expert report, you address the question of whether it is possible that persons could have nitrate deposits on their hands of they have manual contact with objects that have previously been exposed to reaction clouds of military explosives. Now did you perform any experiments to test whether contamination can result from manual contact with substances?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, we did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could you describe how you perform these tests?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: The substances were put into contact with hand, with a hand, and then we used cling film to take a sample of the traces from the hand, and we sprayed this cling film with the diphenylamine reagent, with a soaking time of a couple of minutes, and after that, the test proved positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And from what you know, is the method you used in this test comparable to the method used when performing the paraffin glove test?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: The paraffin test is -- uses wax, and cling film uses cling film. But it's only a sampling method of the traces that remain on the hand. And of course the two are comparable.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Could you tell us what substances, if any, returns a positive result using this test?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: I carried out the test with -- with fertilisers on a nitrate basis that was pure ammonium nitrate so it would be expected, to be expected that there would be a strong positive reaction. Then we used it on rust, where we just used scrap steel and put it in contact with a hand, took samples. Again, there was a positive test, but before there's a positive reaction everything has to be resolved and when the test is done on rust, it is a little bit more difficult. You don't find as much -- the test will be positive but not as strongly positive as the ones before. Then we used it on curing -- cured foodstuffs, salami and ham, and here it is to be expected that the test would be positive but only sporadically, so it is not evenly distributed because there's not a lot of nitrate in curing salts. There's about 100 milligrams per kilogramme of meat of nitrite. Those two were positive as well, and then we took samples of explosive residues, for TNT residues, for example, from an exploded hand-grenade from Yugoslavia, there was 100 grams of TNT as an explosive substance and the many fragments were touched by a hand and samples were taken and, again, there was a positive result sporadically which we expected. PETN, penthrite residues from the M75 hand-grenades here, again, we had a positive result. In this case there was a question of self-made bomb, hand-grenade, an IED, and the reaction was very positive. There was, in the residues that we sampled, there was a lot of explosive substance left. Then gunpowder residues, there, we just burned the powder off which is the same as what happens inside the grenade and because it was burned off and it was not under pressure we had a lot of non-burned particles which led to a very positive test. And then finally, we used a substance that was shot at from 25 centimetres and that was immediately sprayed with reagent and again there was this uneven distribution and here you can see at sight how small the particles are within this shoot -- firing area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. And, again, from your experience would this be an exhaustive list of substances that you would expect to return a positive result from manual contact?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Well, it's more than that, but I haven't done all 20 tests. It's a logical corollary that, of course, that would work as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if we could please see page 27 of the exhibit which is currently up, Exhibit P431, that has ERN N002-5825. Sorry, we're looking for page 27. It should be the page before this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Doctor, what does the photograph on the screen in front of you show?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: That's the test we did with gunpowder, but we shook out the gunpowder, half a gramme, say, and we just fired it, and brought the residue in contact with the hand and then we took samples. And that's why it is so strongly positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can we go to page 22 of the same exhibit, which is ERN N002-5820. And can I have -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Doctor, what does this photograph show?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: That's a sampling from rust with normal ion particles and there's rust on the surface and these particles were touched very briefly by a hand. Rust is absorbed very quickly. It's iron oxide. And then samples were taken and sprayed with the reagent and as expected, the test was positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So, Doctor, the scattering of light blue spots that we see on the outline of the hand here, these indicate particles that have tested positive?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, these are rust particles.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can we turn now to page 25 of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Doctor, what does this photograph show?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: That was residue from TNT on an exploded hand-grenade. M52 from Yugoslavia contains TNT. And here we had an unevenly distributed positive result.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could you describe exactly how the manual contact was made in this particular test?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: There were many hand-grenade fragments that were collected, over 100, I think, and they were put into a dish, and these particles were touched by a hand and then the samples were taken with adhesive film.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So this is simply done by picking up fragments of an exploded hand-grenade?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And on the test we see two blue spots and these are the spots that indicate TNT particles; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, based on your experience, if a positive diphenylamine test is produced, what sort of test would then need to be done in order to establish the precise source of that positive result?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Well, then you need to continue. We have a forensic technique that's been well proven and now we need to use a procedure which identifies the substances that have come up in the colour test, and in our department we use the OCMS -- MS method, liquid chromatography mass spectrometry, it's a method which is more sensitive than diphenylamine by an exponent of five to ten, and it not only works with colour detection. It produces mass fragments and you can exactly pinpoint from what origin they come. And this only -- that's the only possibility to say with certainty whether it was TNT or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And that would likewise refer to nitrate or gunpowder particles.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we would do. Well, that is our job. We must always be able to find 100 per cent proof of what substance has been fired or burned or ignited, and if we don't find a result, you can't draw conclusions. You have no proof.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now I'd just like to ask you a few hypothetical situations and this is based on your experience and what have you testified to and what is contained in your report. If people were in a relatively small area such as a village shells and mortars exploding in that area would it be possible for people other than those firing such weapons to be contaminated by touching objects that had been contaminated also in that area?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's perfectly possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Could people become contaminated through being touched by others who had such particles on their hands?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: That's possible too, because these contaminants are not burned into the skin. They're just loosely on the surface of the hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could persons become contaminated if they were hit or struck with fire-arms or other weapons?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: What do you mean by "hit"?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If a weapon was used to strike a person's hand, arm or other part of the body, could particles, nitrate particles then end up on that person's body?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, especially when shells are fired, cartridges.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarified what I meant there. Now, is it also possible that persons could become contaminated if they were transported in vehicles where weapons had already been transported?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: It's always a hypothetical possibility to be in contact with residue in a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if people were to become contaminated in any of these ways that we've just discussed if they were tested using a diphenylamine test, would it return a positive result for nitrates or for oxidizing agents?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Oh, yes, absolutely. Inasmuch as there's sufficient of the substance possible, because there is always a detection limit and when you go across the detection limit, then the test will be positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if we can just go back to the photograph which is on the screen in front of you. This is it the result from the diphenylamine test where a person picked up a fragment of an exploded grenade, and here we can see two particles on the adhesive glove taken from that hand. Now would this be comparable to what you might expect to see if a person had become contaminated in any of the ways that we've just talked about?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes. It won't be distributed over the entire surface of the hand. There will be small particles present and this is to do with the reaction of the explosive. Just imagine how this works. If the explosive is made into a hand-grenade in a cartridge the reaction starts but it doesn't reach full velocity, only after a few microseconds is it at full velocity. So all traces wherever the cartridge was, in that area, there you have strong presence of residue. But it is already detonated then you have hardly any residue left at all on the fragments and it is difficult to distinguish the two. You just need to be lucky. You always have to look at the fragments of the hand-grenade where you can find the winding, the thread, and the detonators are. That's where you have the biggest chance of finding explosive residue. In other parts, it will always be difficult. And then of course not all explosives, nitrates are the same, we happen to touch two particles by hand with high amounts of residue, and two that weren't so that's why it is so unevenly distributed over the hand. That is quite a typical picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So would it be correct that any type of contact that we're been talking about, it is much more likely that would you a small number of particles, such as in this photo, rather than a much larger number?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And would it be possible that you would see a similar sort of result of a few particles on the back of a person's hand as well as on the palm?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Depending on where the contamination happened on the hand, yes. You can't foretell. Wherever the contact took place, that's where I will find a positive reaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I have no more questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Doctor. I have a few questions for you, but before that I would like to introduce you to my lead counsel, Ms. Edina Residovic, and together we are representing Mr. Boskoski. Doctor, you have indicated in your report and in your evidence in chief the limitations of the diphenylamine test. In particular, in regard to its ability to identify the exact origin of the particle that has been identified. And you have also indicated that to ensure greater certainty in that regard you would need to combine this test with a mechanism of visual identification. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Not visual identification, but instrumental, analytical, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this instrumental or analytical identification mechanism, there are quite a few, is that correct, Doctor, some more reliable than others?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think your answer was not picked by the transcript, if you could repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Could you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The question was this instrumental or analytical identification mechanism, there are quite a few, is that correct, Doctor, some more reliable than others?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, Doctor --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware, Doctor, what particular identification mechanism had been used by the Macedonian authorities in this particular case?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes. We used a microscope.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Doctor, if the --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Used --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the Macedonian experts who carried out those tests were to suggest that they, thanks to their experience and professional abilities were able to identify or to distinguish between different type of particles, you would have no reason to challenge that assertion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: That's a difficult question, because I don't use microscopic analysis. That is not my area of expertise, to find microscopic proof, and I'm not the right person to answer that question. Dr. Eichner was here a couple of days ago. He does a lot of microscopic work. And there are some possibilities, okay, I'm not an expert. I can give you a position, but I'm not an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in that case I will move on from this area of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will simply draw the Chamber's attention to submissions that were made on the 20th of June of 2007 at page 2436 and 2437 in relation to an application by the Prosecution to withdraw Ms. Kunovska as an expert, and I'm sure that the Chamber is well aware of the submissions that were made at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Doctor, did you have any information at the time about the nature or origin of the nitrite particles relevant to the Ljuboten case? Did you have information as to where those particles had originated from?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Doctor, did you have any information as to the means of transmission which was relevant to this particular case or not?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: No. I just received information from Dr. Eichner that there was strong shelling of a small village, and that the procedures used by the Macedonian police with sampling and so on, what procedures they had used. In written form, very briefly, I had a one-page information.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Doctor. You have given evidence about the number of particles which could or would or might be found on a person's body parts and you have indicated that, depending on the substance which would be analysed, the number of particles could vary. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also -- thank you, Doctor. Is it also correct that the number of particles that would be observed at the time of the test could be the result of external factors such as the weather, if it rains for instance, or the activities of the person being tested. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes. Because these residues, as much as they are not ignited, are loosely distributed, and if there is strong wind or weather conditions you can lose the traces.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Doctor, you have been shown a number of pictures already and I would like to show you three more.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown what is 1D4 -- I'm sorry, 1D545.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Doctor, are you familiar with the appearance of propellant which are to be found in cartridges?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Doctor, if the picture ever appears, I will ask you a question about this particular matter.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you familiar, Doctor, with that type of propellant? Is that a type of propellant that you had seen before?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it looks. Propellant has various forms and we have the cylindrical forms and this only is used for firing, to propel the projectile from the weapon. And depending on how high the speed this is, the more the propellant differs. This is because the larger the surface, the faster does the shot come from the weapon. And because there are various possibilities there are different kinds of propellant. You can determine with what speed the projectile has left the weapon, and depending on that, the surfaces will differ.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree, Doctor, that this particular picture of propellant is a picture of propellant that has not been burned. In other words, it is intact propellant as you would find it in a cartridge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated, Doctor, that there are different sorts of propellant that can be found in cartridges. Is that correct, however, that in a single cartridge the propellant would in fact be consistent in size and shape as is the case with this picture?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes. The same charge would be used for the same firing arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the witness could now please be shown what is 1D546, please. We will come back to this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Doctor, would you agree on the picture that have you in front of you, that this is quite a common visual appearance of burned, and for some of them partly burned, and in one case unaffected propellant grain from a cartridge. Is that a visual appearance or visual image that you're familiar with?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct, Doctor, that after a bullet has been fired, it is quite common to have that pattern of some propellant particles being burned, some unburned and some completely combusted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, that happens.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And such observation as to the state of the particles in question may be done by visual inspection, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Well, if you know the background you could draw that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Including with a microscope. Is that correct, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes. If you do that kind of test often as is always the case in life, one gains experience, and then the pictures tell their story.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to go back to the previous picture, Doctor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the Registry could assist. It's 1D454.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's another picture, Doctor, I'd like to show you. It would be the second page, please. Thank you very much. Doctor, is it correct that particles of TNT are, so to say, flake-like in appearance such as the ones that appear on your screen right now?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, it can be the case or not, because TNT is used in various forms. There are these flaky forms but it can be compressed as well. In hand-grenades, it's compressed. Just think: The more compact the sample, the faster will it convert.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct, Doctor, that in a single -- I apologise to the interpreters. Is that correct, Doctor, that within a single explosive charge the different particles of TNT explosive would vary greatly in size and shape as is demonstrated by this picture. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have no further question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Just a matter, if we could tender both pictures. They are 1D545 and 1D546, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter numbers 1D00545 and 1D00546 will become exhibit numbers 1D148 and 1D149 respectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Dr. Klaus Stein. My name is Antonio Apostolski and together with my colleague Jasmina Zivkovic we appear on behalf of Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Doctor, you stated hypothetically that it was possible for the persons who were subjected, who were in an area where there was huge shelling, who were transported in cars where weapons were transported and those who were hit by rifle-butts, that it was possible that they were contaminated by nitrate particles. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now whether it is correct that if several persons, for instance, some 30 persons, were subjected to the same circumstances, such as I mentioned before, so having been present in an area of shelling, having been transported in same cars, and having been hit with rifle-butts, would that mean that all of them would have residues of nitrates?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: If they had direct contact with the substance, it is possible, but the essential factor is the contact for the test to function.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that out of 33 people who were in the same circumstances such as I have mentioned before, just on 16 of them nitrate particles were shown, would that mean that just those 16 out of the whole lot had contact with the nitrate particles, although they were subjected to the same circumstances of stay, movement, and circumstances such as having been hit with rifle-butts?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS STEIN
utterances.text: This would show simply that the -- the people with a negative test result were not -- did not come in contact with the nitrate particles.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I have no further questions at this time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, you will be pleased to hear that this brings your examination to an end. You are now free to go. Thank you very much for your help.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The Prosecution's next witness is Albanian speaking and because of the demands of other trials, it is my understanding there is no interpreter, Albanian interpreter available today, due to scheduling. It was not anticipated that this witness would take -- would be so short. Therefore, with the consent of the Chamber, we will call our next witness, Mr. Rexhepi, tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Okay. We will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 7th day of September, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.10 a.m.,
